factual_methodology.summary: Cross-checked TSE first-round certified shares, dates and voting schedule, ICI money-market assets, US Treasury 2/10/30 year constant maturity rates, Brent and WTI settlement historical records, S&P Global flash PMI releases, September Japanese CPI, UK ONS retail volumes, and Brazilian government fiscal planning/autonomy rules. Source and observation vintages identified.

research_depth.summary: Six independently meaningful H2 analytic sections per language, greater than 1700 substantive words excluding visual fences and URLs. New fiscal implementation section is supported by federal government PPA/LOA source.

evidence_traceability.summary: 15 numbered citations in both languages with matching source URLs, including direct Japan September 2026 statistical release and the correct dated individual energy futures historical quotes. Contemporary oil market prices do not prove real physical oil loss.

counterfactual_review.summary: Election outcome not predicted, Sunday market prices not invented, oil spot/settlement distinction explicit, global oil/geopolitical shock differentiated from actual delivery losses, money-market assets not treated as identifiable portfolio shifts.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Two distinct bar charts (Brazil first-round valid vote shares and Brent/WTI USD per barrel), plus material evidence table, causal flow and geographic transmission map. Quantitative series identical EN and PT-BR, incomparable units not added.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Reviewed r2 PT-BR body copyedit: replaced 'Esta análise não pressupõe vencedor.' with a directly stated pre-count election limitation. No self-referential 'este/esta artigo/relatório/análise/pesquisa' strings remain in public prose. Earlier six evidence-grounded sections and the English edition unchanged.

contrary_evidence: The 4 October first-round lead does not forecast the 25 October runoff winner.
The Brent–WTI spread does not separately identify a Gulf shipping risk premium.
Elevated U.S. flash PMI output and rising money-market assets coexist with other possible liquidity interpretations; these data do not identify investor trades.
British third-quarter retail volume increase differs in period from September's monthly contraction.
limitations: Review concerns an early-Sunday 05:00 BRT snapshot, not later election-night outcomes or live market moves.
Some secondary energy shipping security and oil sentiment remain narrative risk descriptions rather than verified physical disruption measurements.
The market-price history source is a secondary trading-data service rather than an exchange-certified final contract settlement.
Site deployment, live availability and crawl visibility require downstream independent build verification.
notes: r2 copy-edit verification corrects exactly one PT-BR self-reference rejected by public validator; quantitative data, sources, EN and all prior independent factual/evidence checks unchanged; binds to PT and pending new source hashes.

en.title: Global Macro — Brazil votes while a Gulf oil premium waits for the next market opening
en.deck: Brazil's Sunday runoff creates a closed-market political information shock as Friday's crude futures reflect renewed Gulf shipping risk; the cross-asset transmission depends on fiscal institutions, dollar yields and physical throughput.
en.regime: Weekend political information shock alongside elevated dollar financing costs and Gulf energy-transport risk.
en.key_risk: Conflating an unobserved Brazilian election result and reported Gulf threats with verified asset repricing or physical oil supply losses.
